question: Can three absolute-state abundances expose time-varying net state loss despite unknown constant growth, and how much precision does this require?
scope: Synthetic measurement-design study, not a patient model, treatment schedule or new cancer mechanism. Version 1 is preserved.
equations: b(t)=b_inf*(1-exp(-t/tau)) under the alternative; b is constant under the null
time_unit: Hypothetical sensitive-cell doubling time; not days or drug doses.
source_status: Reversible tolerance and state switching are source-motivated. ALL parameter values, ranges and noise levels are hypothetical, not fitted from patients, the molecular data or cited papers.
observation_times: 0,T,2T for each fixed T in [0.5,1,2]; no final-test time-window selection
measurement_model: Independent mean-unbiased lognormal abundance measurements; known common log variance log(1+CV^2). Average logs across independent replicate wells at each time. State abundance is directly measured with a validated functional label. No count zeros or label errors in the primary model.
absolute_state_test: Two-sided Gaussian level .05; reject |C| > z(.975)*sqrt(6*log(1+CV^2)/r). Under constant net P growth, expected C=0 even with unknown initial abundance, gP and b.
bulk_test: Compute the min and max of noiseless C_N over a prespecified constant-b composition grid. Reject if C_N is below min-z(.975)*SD or above max+z(.975)*SD. This is a conservative finite-grid composite-null envelope, not an optimal bulk test or proof of control over continuous parameters.

heldout_null.parameter_distribution: Independent uniform draws within the bulk-null grid bounds, shared across fixed T/noise/r settings
heldout_null.report: Each case's false-positive rate and binomial Monte Carlo standard error, plus maxima and median. Off-grid null curvatures are checked against the grid envelope.

alternative_power.analytic: Evaluate exact Gaussian power for both tests and compare with Monte Carlo; summarize all cases, not only favorable ones.

equal_cost_scope: Both designs use the same three observation times and replicate count. Equal actual money, effort or attainable precision between total and state-resolved abundance assays is NOT assumed.
specificity_challenges: No switching with time-varying P growth gP(t)=gP-b_inf*(1-exp(-t/tau)) gives exactly the same P trajectory.
Constant biological growth with time-varying marker retention m(t)=exp(-b_inf*(t-tau*(1-exp(-t/tau)))) gives exactly the same labeled P trajectory.

heteroscedastic_stress.report: False positives if the common-CV=.1 formula is naively used, versus correction using the known three log variances and mean-log biases. This is a prespecified model-misspecification stress, not a biological-memory result.

analytic_targets: Derive contrast noise SD=sqrt(6)*sigma/sqrt(r). Solve minimum positive contrast for 80 percent power under the two-sided test, and report all CV/r settings.
Derive the tau/T maximizing C at fixed b_inf and T by solving exp(x)=2*x+1 for positive x=T/tau. This is an analytic sensitivity identity, not a treatment timing recommendation.
controls: Compare closed-form P and C_P with independent ODE integration over every alternative and time window.
Constant-b null C_P=0; analytic constant-b total abundance checked against ODE at boundary cases.
Tighter ODE tolerances must preserve contrasts within 1e-7.
Validate exact P-trajectory equivalence of the two specificity challenges; never interpret curvature as specific evidence of memory.
Report Gaussian analytic-vs-Monte-Carlo differences and uncertainty; do not tune thresholds after held-out tests.
limitations: Independent constant-CV lognormal assay noise with known variance is an idealization; biological replicate heterogeneity, count zeros, density effects and correlated measurement errors are absent.
Three-point curvature rejects constant net state growth only. Time-varying growth, marker drift, state re-entry and unobserved states can produce signals.
No functional tolerant-cell marker is validated here; the project's 17-gene score is not treated as one.
No comparison with all possible bulk inference methods; the conservative envelope deliberately permits unknown composition and constant rates.
Grid-averaged power is not a real-world frequency or mechanism probability.
novelty: State switching, memory, growth-curve inference and experimental design have substantial prior art. Scientific novelty of this exact formula/comparison is unestablished. The useful target is transparent quantitative measurement guidance and failure boundaries.
